## Examples {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
#| fig-cap: "Levene's Test for Homogeneity of Variance"
#| label: fig-levene-test

# Create sample data with different variances
set.seed(123)
group1 <- rnorm(50, mean = 10, sd = 1)      # smaller variance
group2 <- rnorm(50, mean = 10, sd = 2)      # larger variance
group3 <- rnorm(50, mean = 10, sd = 1.5)    # medium variance

# Combine into a data frame
data <- data.frame(
  values = c(group1, group2, group3),
  group = rep(c("Group1", "Group2", "Group3"), each = 50)
)

# Run Levene's test
library(car)
result_levene <- leveneTest(values ~ group, data = data)
print("Levene's Test for Homogeneity of Variance:")
print(result_levene)

# Interpretation:
# If p-value > 0.05: we fail to reject the null hypothesis (variances are homogeneous)
# If p-value < 0.05: we reject the null hypothesis (variances are NOT homogeneous)
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
#| fig-cap: "Bartlett's Test for Homogeneity of Variance"
#| label: fig-bartlett-test

# Run Bartlett's test on the same data
result_bartlett <- bartlett.test(values ~ group, data = data)
print("Bartlett's Test for Homogeneity of Variance:")
print(result_bartlett)

# Interpretation:
# If p-value > 0.05: we fail to reject the null hypothesis (variances are homogeneous)
# If p-value < 0.05: we reject the null hypothesis (variances are NOT homogeneous)

# Note: Levene's test is more robust to non-normality, while Bartlett's test is more sensitive
# to departures from normality but also more powerful when data are normally distributed.
```

```{r}
#| code-fold: false
#| fig-cap: "Boxplot and Density Plot Comparing Distribution and Variance"
#| label: fig-variance-plots

# Set up 1x2 panel layout
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# Panel 1: Boxplot
boxplot(values ~ group, data = data,
        main = "Boxplot: Distribution by Group",
        xlab = "Group",
        ylab = "Values",
        col = c("lightblue", "lightcoral", "lightgreen"),
        border = "black",
        lwd = 1.5)

# Panel 2: Density plot
plot(density(group1), main = "Density Plot: Distribution by Group",
     xlab = "Values", ylab = "Density",
     col = "blue", lwd = 2, xlim = c(4, 16))
lines(density(group2), col = "red", lwd = 2)
lines(density(group3), col = "green", lwd = 2)
legend("topright",
       legend = c("Group1 (sd=1)", "Group2 (sd=2)", "Group3 (sd=1.5)"),
       col = c("blue", "red", "green"),
       lwd = 2,
       cex = 0.8)

# Reset plot layout
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
